history.text:
Short answer: a new ball comes second. Fix the spare game first, then fill the gap in your bag.

Spares first: you made 22 of 39, and your 10 pin is your top leave. A real spare ball (plastic, polished, no hook) would help more than another strike ball. Your specs are unknown, so a plastic ball drilled for spares gives you a straight, repeatable line for the 10 and 7 pins.

Resurface second: the Slingshot is high gloss and very low flare, and your 18→14 and 19→11 lines show it's short on hook. A light 2000 to 3000 Abralon, or a 1500 if you want more length, can add some midlane read. Ask your pro shop first.

The new ball gap: both of your strike balls are low-flare, symmetric, and clean. Your 10 pin and light misses (17 of 65) show you need more backend and more forgiveness. Look for a medium-to-heavy oil, asymmetric or high-differential core, with a solid reactive cover and a 2000-grit finish. It should sit between the Concept and Slingshot on early read, with a stronger, more angular backend than either. That adds hold in the oil and a lot more recovery on light hits.

Example models, though my product knowledge may be a year or two out of date, so confirm current lineups at a pro shop:
Storm Phaze series
Hammer Black Widow series
Motiv Venom Shock type

Treat the small line samples carefully. Your 20→12 line (9 of 22) is your best repeatable shot.

advice-ball.text: The biggest gap is the spare ball, not another strike ball. Its specs are unknown, and your 10 pin is your top leave (8 times). A plastic or polished spare ball drilled for a straight line would make the 10 and 7 pin more repeatable. Example models, though my product knowledge may be dated: Storm Match Up, Pro-Am Plastic by Ebonite, and Hammer Spare. A resurface of the Slingshot matters second, since it is high gloss with low hook. Fix spares first, then reassess the bag.

history.text:
Main line: 20 to 12 (stand 20, aim 12) with the Concept. It's your most-used line (22 shots), 9 strikes, and your average entry board is 17.6, right on the 17.5 pocket. It's your repeatable shot. Caveat: 41% strikes is a small sample, so treat it as a starting point.

Move-in ladder (2-and-1: move feet 2 boards, aim 1 board, same direction as the miss):
Start: 20 to 12.
Leaving 10 pins or hitting light/high-side misses as the lane burns: move left. Step 1: 22 to 13. Step 2: 24 to 14. Step 3: 26 to 15.
If you're hitting the pocket but leaving 4s/7s or getting early reaction (ball turning too soon), move right the same way: 18 to 11, then 16 to 10.
Note: 18 to 14 gave 17.8 entry but that angle is a different shape; use it only as a straighter backup.

Ball switches: Start with the Concept on fresh oil. When it starts reading early and hooking too soon (washouts, 4 pin, high leaves), or when you've moved to 24 or beyond, switch to the Slingshot. Its length and low flare let you play 18 to 14 or similar as the oil carries down. Switch back if the Slingshot goes too straight and leaves 10s.

Heavier oil or fresh pair: 24 to 13 with the Concept. Play more direct to give the ball room to hook, though the 5-shot sample is small.

Spare shots to drill most:
1. 10 pin (your top leave, 8 times): spare ball from 32 to 15. Drill this one first.
2. 7 pin (4 times) from 29 to 15 with the spare ball. Repeat until it's automatic.

Also: 51 of your first-ball misses were pocket hits that left pins, so work on consistent ball speed and carry as well. Spare conversion of 30/54 is your biggest score gain.

advice-lines.text:
Main line: with the Concept, stand 22-24 and aim at the 2nd arrow (board 10). Your earlier 20 to 12 line had an average entry of 17.6, on the pocket, so use it as your reference if the lane is fresh or you feel unsure. Tonight your best shots crossed near board 10, so that is your target.

Move-in ladder (move feet 2 boards, aim 1 board, same direction as the miss):
Start: 20 to 12.
Step 1: 22 to 13.
Step 2: 24 to 14.
Step 3: 26 to 15.
Use it when you leave 10 pins or see light or high-side misses as the lane burns. Only move after a repeated miss, not one bad shot.

When to switch balls: go to the Slingshot only if the Concept starts hooking early or leaving 4 or 7 pins on the left side, as the lane breaks down. Its low hook is a late-game option, so treat it as untested.

history.text:
What the data says
Your clearest pattern is spare conversion on a few leaves, not the line. Single-pin spares are 7 of 9, but total spares are 14 of 20, so the misses on multi-pin leaves (3-6-9-10, 3-9-10, 3-6-7-10, 2-4-5) are costing you. Entry reads are 9 light, 17 pocket, 7 high, so light misses outnumber high ones slightly. Stance 20 to target 12 has 8 strikes in 20 shots and an average entry of 17.6, which is on pocket. The other lines have 1 to 11 shots, and the 19 and 22 lines have only 1 each, so don't draw conclusions there. Hook and spread are estimates, and no arrow targets were logged.

Line adjustment
Keep 20 to 12 as your home line. For light hits (ball hitting around the 3-6-9-10 side), use the 2-and-1 rule: move your feet 2 boards left and your target 1 board left, for example 22 to 11. For high hits (7 pin leaves), move feet 2 right and target 1 right, for example 18 to 13. Make one move at a time and give each at least 5 shots. If the Slingshot (later breakpoint) leaves you light or the Concept leaves you high, swap balls before moving far. Both are untested for hook, so compare them on the same line.

Spare work
Your 10 pin appears 3 times and the 4 and 7 pins 2 times each, so practice those with the spare ball. For the 10 pin, stand left and cross to the right corner. For the 7 and 4, stand right and cross left. Use the same spot on the approach each time and adjust only by 1 to 2 boards. Also spend a little time on 3-6-9-10, which shows up twice, by aiming at the 3 pin, though that is a small sample.

Drills for next practice
1. Mark and log 20 shots from stance 20 at target 12 with the Concept. Record whether the ball crosses the arrows on target, left, or right.
2. Repeat 20 shots with the Slingshot on the same line and compare entry reads and strikes.
3. Shoot 10 single-pin spares each for the 10, 4, and 7 pins with the spare ball, 30 shots total, and track the makes.

all.text:
What the data says
First-ball strikes are 44 of 99, and spares are 30 of 54. Single pins are 16 of 23, so the misses are costing you on the 10 pin and multi-pin leaves. Your own debrief says misses are mostly left and due to aim, and focus lapses on the pin and the next bowler match that. Brooklyns (4 of 18) came from crossing the 3rd arrow instead of the 2nd.

Line adjustment
Keep the Concept line near 22-24 to the 2nd arrow. If you keep missing left, do not move your aim; fix your eyes and target first. Move only after two clean shots leave the same result.

Spare work
10 pin: stand 32, aim 15 with the spare ball. 7 pin: stand 29, aim 15. Look at the arrow or a spot, not the pin. Take a full routine on every spare.

Drills

2. Spare 10 pin: 10 shots from 32 at 15, eyes on the mark. Then 10 for the 7 pin from 29.
3. Distraction drill: 10 shots with a teammate moving beside you. Repeat your routine and keep eyes forward each time.

session:2026-10-19_league_lynwood_bowl.text:
What the data says
Your scores fell each game (190, 159, 149), and the strike rate was 13 of 32 overall. Entry reads were light 8, pocket 15, high 9, so you were not tracking one consistent miss. The 27 to 14 line (1 shot, avg entry board 24) and the slower shots (4 strikes in 12) suggest a late or drifting read, but the samples are small, so treat all of this as a hint, not proof. Hook and entry boards are estimates, and only stance and pins are certain. I can't tell exactly when the lane transitioned, because the data isn't split by game.

Line adjustment
The 2-and-1 rule: move your feet 2 boards for every 1 board you move your target, in the direction you want the ball to go. Your 22 and 24 stances averaged entry boards 18 and 18.9, which is near pocket at 17.5, so 22 to 12 is your best-supported starting line. The 24 line averaged 18.9, so it ran about a board high. If you are high, move feet 2 left and target 1 left, for example 24 to 22 with the target going from 12 to 11. If you are light, move feet 2 right and target 1 right. Make the move after the first miss of the pair, not after three. Also try the Slingshot (43 ft breakpoint) as the lane burns up. It was untested enough here that I can't say it helps.

Spare work
You converted 8 of 19 spares, and single-pin spares were only 4 of 7. The 10 pin led your leaves at 4, so prioritize it. Use the spare ball and a straight line from the left side, with your feet moved to the left for the 10 pin. Stay with the same ball for every single-pin spare. The 2-4-10 and 1-2-4 leaves (2 each) are too few to prioritize.

Drills for next practice
1. 10 pin spare: 20 shots, with one cross-lane angle, recording makes.
2. Arrow target: 24 shots at 12 from stance 22, tracking left, right, and hit. Aim for 6 of 8 hits.
3. 2-and-1 moves: 3 sets of 6 shots. Intentionally miss 2 boards, then correct using the rule and check the entry board.

history.text:
What the data says
Scores fell each game: 228, 199, 159. That points to the lane transitioning (oil breaking down) while the ball and line stayed the same. Of 34 first balls, 8 were high (Brooklyn side), 7 were light, and 19 hit the pocket. Strikes were 18 of 34 (53%). Spares were 8 of 15, and single-pin spares were 5 of 7, so missed spares cost you more in games 2 and 3. Caveats: the entry reads are inferred from leaves, the target data is only 1 marked shot, and hook is unknown. Treat all of this as a hint, not a verdict. We don't know which game the misses came in, so "adjustments came too late" is a guess.

Line adjustment
Use the 2-and-1 rule: move your feet 2 boards left and your target 1 board left, which keeps the same breakpoint area while giving the ball more room as the lane burns. For a right-hander, if the ball is hooking early or hitting light, move the other way. Starting point: if leaves are mostly 7 pins (light) after game 1, move feet 2 left and target 1 left. If high hits show up (the 10 pin or 6-10 leaves), move feet 2 right and target 1 right. Make one move at a time and check 2 shots. Next week, consider switching from the Concept (39 ft) to the Slingshot (43 ft) once the front of the lane dries, since the longer breakpoint gives more length. Record your foot and target boards each game.

Spare work
Prioritize the 2 pin (your most common leaf, 3 times), then the 10 pin and 3 pin. Use the spare ball and shoot straight, moving your starting position so the line to the pin is across the lane, not through it. Corner pins are the most common leaf, so keep practice on those. The 6-7-10 split (2 times) is rarely makeable, so don't spend time there.

Drills for next practice
1. Mark one arrow target, throw 10 shots, and record hit, left, or right. Aim for 6 or more hits.
2. Spare ladder: 10 shots each at the 2 pin, 3 pin, and 10 pin with the spare ball. Aim for 7 of 10 on each.
3. Simulate transition: throw 3 games of 5 shots each with the Concept, adjust 2-and-1 after each set based on the leave, and write down the moves.

session:2026-10-26_league_lynwood_bowl.text: Good finish: scores went 159, 199, 228, and strikes went 3, 7, 8. That's real progress from the Concept on 22-24. What improved since the earlier plan: your line is repeating better, and your best shots crossing near board 10 match the pocket. What still needs work: the misses. You said they were mostly left, caused by aim, and 4 of 18 strikes in debriefed games went Brooklyn when you crossed on top of the 3rd arrow instead of the 2nd. Focus also slipped twice: looking at the pin on spares (the F5 10 pin) and at the bowler next door (F8 in game 2, F4 in game 3). Game 1 had a cold-finger gutter ball first ball. Next week: warm your hands before game 1, pick your arrow, and keep your eyes on it until the ball is past the arrows. Treat the leave counts as small samples.
